title: Impact of School District Boundaries on Urban House Prices

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Spatial sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the school-district boundary.
- Why: Houses on either side of a boundary are geographically close and share neighborhood amenities, but differ discretely in school district assignment. The discontinuity in assignment at the boundary identifies the causal impact of being in the less desirable district on log house prices.
- Running variable and treatment: We construct a signed distance to the boundary: negative on the better-district side and positive on the less-desirable side. Treatment is an indicator for being on the less desirable side.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: Potential outcomes (log prices absent treatment) vary smoothly with distance at the boundary; any jump in y at 0 is due to school district assignment.
  - No precise sorting: Households cannot precisely sort at a fine scale right at the boundary (no manipulation of location exactly at 0).
  - Local comparability: Within a small bandwidth, unobservables are similar across sides.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code for boundary RDD on house prices

# 0) Packages
req_pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in req_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Load data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s94_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Inspect and construct signed running variable:
# Make signed distance positive on the less desirable (treated) side and negative on the better side
df$signed_x <- ifelse(df$treated == 1, 1, -1) * df$running_var
# Treatment from signed_x
df$D <- as.integer(df$signed_x >= 0)

# Sanity check: D matches 'treated'
if (any(df$D != df$treated)) {
  stop("Constructed treatment D does not match 'treated' in data.")
}

# 2) Helper: local linear RDD estimator with triangular kernel
estimate_rdd <- function(y, x, p = 1, h = NULL, donut = 0) {
  # y: outcome, x: signed running variable
  # p: polynomial order (1 = linear, 2 = quadratic)
  # h: bandwidth (if NULL, choose a data-driven but simple bandwidth)
  # donut: drop observations with |x| <= donut
  n <- length(y)
  ax <- abs(x)
  if (is.null(h)) {
    # Simple data-driven bandwidth: 30th percentile of |x| (local window)
    h <- as.numeric(quantile(ax, 0.30, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  # Donut-hole exclusion
  keep <- (ax <= h) & (ax > donut)
  if (sum(keep) < 30) stop("Too few observations within bandwidth; adjust h or donut.")
  
  yk <- y[keep]
  xk <- x[keep]
  Dk <- as.integer(xk >= 0)
  axk <- abs(xk)
  # Triangular kernel weights
  wk <- pmax(0, 1 - axk / h)
  
  # Build design matrix for local polynomial with side-specific slopes
  if (p == 1) {
    # y ~ D + x + D:x
    fit <- lm(yk ~ Dk + xk + Dk:xk, weights = wk)
    coef_name <- "Dk"
  } else if (p == 2) {
    xk2 <- xk^2
    fit <- lm(yk ~ Dk + xk + I(xk^2) + Dk:xk + Dk:I(xk^2), weights = wk)
    coef_name <- "Dk"
  } else {
    stop("Only p=1 or p=2 supported.")
  }
  # Robust (HC1) standard errors
  vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
  ct <- lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = vc)
  if (!(coef_name %in% rownames(ct))) stop("Treatment coefficient not found.")
  tau <- as.numeric(ct[coef_name, "Estimate"])
  se  <- as.numeric(ct[coef_name, "Std. Error"])
  z   <- tau / se
  pval <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ci_lo <- tau - 1.96 * se
  ci_hi <- tau + 1.96 * se
  list(
    tau = tau, se = se, z = z, p = pval, ci = c(ci_lo, ci_hi),
    n = sum(keep), h = h, p_order = p, donut = donut
  )
}

# 3) Main RDD estimate (local linear, triangular kernel), bandwidth = 30th pct of |x|
main_res <- estimate_rdd(y = df$y, x = df$signed_x, p = 1, h = NULL, donut = 0)

# 4) Robustness checks
# 4a) Half and double bandwidth
h0 <- main_res$h
res_hhalf  <- estimate_rdd(y = df$y, x = df$signed_x, p = 1, h = 0.5 * h0, donut = 0)
res_hdouble <- estimate_rdd(y = df$y, x = df$signed_x, p = 1, h = 2.0 * h0, donut = 0)

# 4b) Local quadratic
res_quad <- estimate_rdd(y = df$y, x = df$signed_x, p = 2, h = h0, donut = 0)

# 4c) Donut RDD (drop very near the cutoff)
donut_width <- as.numeric(quantile(abs(df$signed_x), 0.02, na.rm = TRUE))
res_donut <- estimate_rdd(y = df$y, x = df$signed_x, p = 1, h = h0, donut = donut_width)

# 4d) Parametric check in a tight neighborhood (using provided near_cutoff indicator)
near_sub <- subset(df, near_cutoff == 1)
# Simple linear-in-distance with side-specific slope (no kernel)
fit_param <- lm(y ~ D + signed_x + D:signed_x, data = near_sub)
vc_param <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit_param, type = "HC1")
ct_param <- lmtest::coeftest(fit_param, vcov. = vc_param)
tau_param <- as.numeric(ct_param["D", "Estimate"])
se_param  <- as.numeric(ct_param["D", "Std. Error"])
ci_param  <- c(tau_param - 1.96 * se_param, tau_param + 1.96 * se_param)
p_param   <- 2 * pnorm(abs(tau_param / se_param), lower.tail = FALSE)

# 5) Print clear numerical results
cat("Boundary RDD: Effect of being in the less desirable district on log house prices\n")
cat("Main local-linear RDD (triangular kernel)\n")
cat(sprintf("  N (within h): %d, bandwidth h: %.4f\n", main_res$n, main_res$h))
cat(sprintf("  Tau (log points): %.4f, SE: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f], p-value: %.4f\n",
            main_res$tau, main_res$se, main_res$ci[1], main_res$ci[2], main_res$p))
cat(sprintf("  Implied price change: %.2f%%\n\n", 100 * (exp(main_res$tau) - 1)))

cat("Robustness checks\n")
cat(sprintf("- Half bandwidth: Tau=%.4f (SE=%.4f), 95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f], p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            res_hhalf$tau, res_hhalf$se, res_hhalf$ci[1], res_hhalf$ci[2], res_hhalf$p, res_hhalf$n))
cat(sprintf("- Double bandwidth: Tau=%.4f (SE=%.4f), 95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f], p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            res_hdouble$tau, res_hdouble$se, res_hdouble$ci[1], res_hdouble$ci[2], res_hdouble$p, res_hdouble$n))
cat(sprintf("- Local quadratic: Tau=%.4f (SE=%.4f), 95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f], p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            res_quad$tau, res_quad$se, res_quad$ci[1], res_quad$ci[2], res_quad$p, res_quad$n))
cat(sprintf("- Donut RDD (drop %.4f around 0): Tau=%.4f (SE=%.4f), 95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f], p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            donut_width, res_donut$tau, res_donut$se, res_donut$ci[1], res_donut$ci[2], res_donut$p, res_donut$n))
cat("\nParametric check in tight neighborhood (near_cutoff==1)\n")
cat(sprintf("  Tau=%.4f (SE=%.4f), 95%% CI=[%.4f, %.4f], p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            tau_param, se_param, ci_param[1], ci_param[2], p_param, nrow(near_sub)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Being in the less desirable district should reduce log house prices near the boundary because buyers capitalize school quality into prices.
- Magnitude: For urban settings, capitalized school-district effects typically range from 5% to 15%. Hence, an expected treatment effect around -0.05 to -0.15 in logs (i.e., a 5–15% price discount) at the boundary. Robustness checks should yield similar negative estimates across reasonable bandwidths and specifications.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the discontinuity at the school district boundary.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Houses in the less desirable school district exhibit lower log prices.
